source: Deep within the entorhinal cortex, grid cells fire in a stunning geometric pattern: as you walk across a room, each neuron activates at multiple locations arranged in a perfect hexagonal lattice, tiling your environment like invisible graph paper. Discovered by May-Britt and Edvard Moser, who earned the 2014 Nobel Prize, these cells function as the brain's internal coordinate system, measuring distance and direction regardless of landmarks. Remarkably, this hexagonal code may extend beyond physical space, mapping abstract concepts and memories too.
